transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-07-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:12
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Head of Security, Horizon Payments); Raj Mehta (Cloud Ops); Priya Singh (Legal)

Summary:
Quick planning session to map SIG/CSF evidence delivery, KMS/encryption responsibilities, audit log exports and residency constraints. Focus on who owns what and timeline for pilot production access.

Topics:
- Evidence spreadsheet + mapping (SIG/CAIQ + custom Horizon form)
- KMS integration model (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed)
- Audit logs, retention, and SIEM ingest
- Data residency and in-flight encryption
- Contracts / attestation timeline

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining. can you all hear me ok?
[00:03] Lena (Horizon): yep loud and clear, thanks. we condensed the questions from our vendor risk team into a master form — i'll drop that in the email after.
[00:08] Maya: perfect, thanks lena. quick intros? i'll hand to samir to say hi from infra / kms side.
[00:13] Samir (Redwood): hi all, samir here, i look after private deployments and kms integrations — mostly the se side. we'll try to keep this practical and map evidence to owners.
[00:19] Raj (Horizon): raj — cloud ops. we run gcp and azure, mixing regions. primary question is whether tokens or pii ever land in redwood-managed storage.
[00:27] Priya (Horizon): priya, contracts. timeline: procurement wants answers before 7/23 for our vendor committee.
[00:33] Maya: ok noted. timeline's tight, so biggest immediate ask is the evidence matrix plus an example audit log extract.
[00:38] Samir: yes, and we have a standard evidence pack we send (SOC 2 report, CAIQ, encryption whitepaper) — i can attach the pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security/evidence-pack
[00:46] Lena: do you have an editable spreadsheet? our team wants to tick boxes and drop evidence links.
[00:49] Maya: yes, we'll push an editable SIG aligned spreadsheet. samir will upload it with prefilled answers for common items.
[00:54] Samir: quick note: sometimes the CAIQ auto-fill has mislabels — uhm like 'key rotation' rows get conflated between customer kms and redwood-managed keys — we'll annotate.
[01:02] Raj: that mismatch is exactly what we worry about. for our architecture, keys must live in customer KMS unless we agree otherwise. do you support BYOK? any HSM integrations?
[01:10] Samir: yes, we support both -- BYOK via customer KMS (cloud KMS like GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and we also offer Redwood-managed keys stored in an HSM. but there are tradeoffs: with our managed keys we handle rotation and low-friction onboarding; with BYOK, the customer retains envelope encryption control but initial config is heavier.
[01:26] Priya: can you confirm if Redwood-managed keys ever leave the HSM in plain text or are they used only for envelope encryption?
[01:31] Samir: they never leave the HSM plaintext — used for wrapping/unwrapping only. i'll put the HSM attestation doc in the pack.
[01:36] Maya: also want to call out our typical deployment modes: hosted api (tokens pass through and ephemeral caches), dedicated (reserved GPU pools where we can offer VPC peering), and private (customer-managed control plane). which mode is horizon targeting?
[01:48] Lena: we're evaluating dedicated first, maybe private later. procurement wants to know data residency constraints — we need logs and stored content to remain in EMEA for certain lanes.
[01:56] Samir: understood. on dedicated we can pin model serving in a region and ensure data plane is in customer's VPC or region depending on setup. for hosted we have limited region controls.
[02:05] Raj: what about memory traces or KV cache? can anything leak into other tenants?
[02:09] Samir: no, tenancy separation is enforced; KV cache is per-tenant. but worth noting that for some performance features we do prefix caching — which is always scoped to customer and not shared.
[02:18] Lena: ok, for the evidence pack, can you include a sample audit log with fields? our SIEM expects: timestamp, request_id, model_name, user_id (pseudonymized ok), operation, response_status, region, latency_ms.
[02:30] Samir: yes, we can produce a synthetic audit export with those columns. we'll also show how logs stream to a customer SIEM via syslog or cloud pubsub.
[02:38] Maya: there's a gotcha — redwood logs contain metadata about prompts for troubleshooting, but we can toggle redaction and retention per customer policy. default retention is 30 days in hosted; dedicated/private can be set to customer policy.
[02:50] Raj: so we can request 90 day retention in dedicated and push to our SIEM for longterm? we don't want prompts stored in redwood's longterm blob.
[02:58] Samir: yes, for dedicated/private you can configure retention and also opt-out of storing request text; we can store only token counts and metadata if required.
[03:07] Priya: legal question — do you have contractual language for data residency? like specific region commitments and audit rights?
[03:13] Maya: we do. we have a data residency addendum that lists region commitment levels and audit clauses; i'll add that doc link to the evidence pack.
[03:18] Priya: perfect. also, is there SOC 2 and do you provide bridge letters for the period between attestations?
[03:24] Samir: we have SOC 2 Type II current through 2026 Q2; yes we provide bridge letters summarizing controls unchanged since audit — we'll include that.
[03:31] Lena: on identity, we use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. can we sync roles so Redwood maps our groups to RBAC roles?
[03:38] Samir: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM. we can map your groups to Redwood RBAC roles (admin, engineer, viewer), and we log admin actions for audit.
[03:47] Raj: does SCIM sync user attributes like region or cost center? we want tags on requests for billing/backtrace.
[03:53] Samir: SCIM syncs standard attributes; for custom attributes we have a mapping table we can configure. we'll share examples.
[03:58] Maya: dropping a note: link to SCIM guide: https://redwood.example.com/docs/scim
[04:02] Lena: thanks. regarding encryption at rest — do you encrypt ephemeral caches and KV at rest with customer-managed keys?
[04:10] Samir: ephemeral KV lives encrypted at rest; with BYOK we can use customer keys for at-rest encryption; with managed keys we encrypt with our keys in HSM and envelope with HSM key.
[04:20] Priya: what about forensic access? if regulator requests logs, what's the process? is there an audit trail of who exported what and when?
[04:27] Samir: yes, exports are logged with an export event; we can produce audit evidence showing the export request, actor (email), timestamp, and an md5/signed checksum of the export bundle.
[04:36] Raj: ok that's good. can you also show a demo of the export UI? we may want automation via API to pull logs hourly.
[04:43] Samir: we have both UI and API. i'll demo the API in the follow-up session and provide a sample curl for pulling logs.
[04:50] Maya: timeline recap: procurement needs answers by 7/23 so our deliverables should land before 7/17 to give you time to review.
[04:57] Lena: yes, please. can you also annotate the SIG row for 'encryption key ownership' to be explicit about who rotates keys?
[05:04] Samir: i'll mark that: rotation responsibility toggles based on BYOK vs managed. we'll show rotation cadence and rotation proofs (kek rotation logs).
[05:12] Priya: is there an NDA or attestation needed before you share certain infra diagrams with us?
[05:17] Maya: we usually share redacted diagrams freely; for detailed infra with IP maps we sign an NDA. i can send a mutual nda template today.
[05:24] Lena: one more risk question — data residency for EU customers: can you guarantee processing and storage stay in eu-west1? we need that spelled out.
[05:31] Samir: yes for dedicated/pvt we can pin infra to eu-west1; for hosted we have multi-region endpoints but we can route by policy — i'll include a routing policy doc.
[05:38] Raj: ok on the demo/next session — we'd like a technical deep dive on KMS integration and log export automation. can we get a 60 minute slot with your infra lead?
[05:45] Maya: absolutely. samir and i will coordinate; propose week of 7/20 — you ok with 7/21 09:00 UTC?
[05:53] Lena: 7/21 works for us.
[05:56] Priya: procurement will want pricing for dedicated vs hosted for the pilot — is that something you can send?
[06:02] Maya: yes, i'll have our AE pricing sheet and the dedicated capacity commit options over to you. note that pricing is approximate until sizing benchmarks.
[06:10] Raj: are benchmarks something you can run against our prompt sets? we might hand over a small sample set.
[06:15] Samir: yes we can run an evaluation — minimal data required; we can run locally in your VPC for private deploy or in our dedicated environment for latency/cost numbers.
[06:24] Lena: ok to proceed. last quick point — evidence delivery format: spreadsheet, pdf attachments, log sample, and optionally signer attestations. prefer all in single shared drive folder.
[06:34] Maya: we'll create a shared folder and populate it. samir will drop the sample logs and the HSM docs; i'll put the contractual addendum and the editable spreadsheet.
[06:42] Maya: any other questions before we wrap?
[06:44] Priya: none from me. thanks.
[06:47] Raj: no, good session. appreciate the clarity.
[06:49] Lena: thanks — looking forward to the evidence pack.

Recap / Next Steps (from call):
